topics.title: Geometric Construction Skills
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: draw perpendicular and parallel lines. (k, s)
construct perpendiculars, angle bisectors, mediators and parallel lines. (u, s)
use a pair of compasses and a ruler to construct special angles. (60°, 45°) (u, s)
relate parallel lines, perpendicular bisector, angle bisector, straight line and a circle as loci. (k, u)
construct geometrical figures such as triangle, square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: Builders, carpenters and tailors need straight edges, right angles and equal lengths. A builder marking out the corners of a house uses strings and pegs to get right angles. In this topic you will learn to draw and construct accurate lines, angles and shapes.
Drawing and constructing

Drawing uses a ruler, a protractor and a set square to measure. Constructing uses only a ruler (for straight lines) and a pair of compasses (for arcs). Constructions are more accurate because they do not depend on reading a scale. Always use a sharp pencil and leave your construction arcs showing.

Parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet, like the two edges of a ruler. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (90°), like the corner of a door frame. You can draw both with a ruler and a set square: slide the set square along the ruler to draw parallel lines.
Measuring lengths and angles

Measure lengths in centimetres and millimetres. Start from the 0 mark on the ruler, not the end of the ruler. To measure an angle, put the centre of the protractor on the vertex (the corner point). Line up the zero line with one arm of the angle. Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm.
Basic constructions
A mediator, or perpendicular bisector, cuts a line segment into two equal halves at right angles. An angle bisector cuts an angle into two equal angles.

body.title: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB
steps: Draw a line segment AB, 8 cm long.
Open the compasses to more than half of AB, for example 5 cm.
With the point on A, draw an arc above and below the line.
Keep the same radius. With the point on B, draw arcs that cross the first two arcs.
Label the crossing points P and Q.
Draw a straight line through P and Q. It meets AB at its midpoint, at 90°.

body.title: Bisect an angle
steps: Draw any angle with vertex O.
With the point on O, draw an arc that cuts both arms. Label the cuts X and Y.
With the point on X, draw an arc inside the angle.
With the same radius and the point on Y, draw an arc that crosses the last one at Z.
Draw a line from O through Z. This line bisects the angle.

body.text: To construct a line through a point P parallel to a line AB, first construct a perpendicular from P to AB. Then construct a second perpendicular at P. Two lines that are both perpendicular to the same line are parallel.
Constructing special angles
A 60° angle comes from an equilateral triangle, where every angle is 60°. Bisecting angles you already have gives new ones.

body.title: Construct angles of 60° and 45°
steps: Draw a line and mark a point O on it.
With the point on O, draw a large arc that cuts the line at A.
With the same radius and the point on A, draw an arc that cuts the first arc at B.
Join O to B. Angle AOB = 60°.
For 45°, first construct a perpendicular at O, which gives 90°.
Then bisect the 90° angle. Each half is 45°.

body.speech: half of sixty degrees is thirty degrees, and half of ninety degrees is forty-five degrees

body.text: In the same way, 120° is two 60° angles side by side, and 22.5° is half of 45°.
Loci
A locus is the set of all points that obey a rule. The plural is loci. Many loci are lines and circles you can construct.

items: Points a fixed distance from a fixed point form a circle.
Points the same distance from two fixed points form the perpendicular bisector of the line joining them.
Points a fixed distance from a straight line form two lines parallel to it.
Points the same distance from two lines that meet form the bisector of the angle between them.
A point moving in one fixed direction traces a straight line.

body.text: For example, a goat tied to a peg with a rope 3 m long can reach every point inside a circle of radius 3 m. Two boreholes are dug in a village. Every point the same distance from both lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line between them.
Constructing polygons and other figures
A polygon is a flat shape with straight sides, such as a triangle, square or hexagon. A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal.

body.title: Construct a triangle with sides 7 cm, 6 cm and 5 cm
steps: Draw the longest side, AB = 7 cm.
Open the compasses to 6 cm. With the point on A, draw an arc above AB.
Open the compasses to 5 cm. With the point on B, draw an arc that crosses the first arc at C.
Join AC and BC. Measure them to check they are 6 cm and 5 cm.

items: Square: draw one side, construct 90° at each end, and mark equal sides with the compasses.
Rectangle: as for the square, but the two pairs of sides have different lengths.
Rhombus: all four sides are equal; use the same compass radius from two corners to find the fourth corner.
Parallelogram: draw two sides at the given angle, then use arcs equal to the opposite sides to find the fourth corner.
Regular hexagon: draw a circle, then step the same radius six times around it and join the marks.

body.title: Loci on the school field
body.text: Work outside in groups with a long string and some sticks or stones as markers. One learner holds the string at a fixed point while another walks keeping it tight; mark the path. Then place two stones and mark many points that are the same distance from both. Describe the shape of each locus and name it.
When you step the radius of a circle around its edge, you get exactly six marks. Why six? What does this have to do with the 60° angle?

Constructions use only a ruler and compasses, and the arcs are left showing. Bisecting angles turns 60° into 30° and 90° into 45°. A locus is the set of points that obey a rule, such as a circle, a perpendicular bisector or an angle bisector.
